name: PixelLab
summary: AI generator for pixel art game assets: characters, 4/8-direction rotations, text- and skeleton-based sprite animations, tilesets, maps and UI elements.
pricing: Free trial tier (no credit card). Paid plans listed at $12/month (2,000 generations), $24/month (5,000) and $50/month (10,000). API usage priced separately per call.
license: Pricing page lists "Use generated images commercially" and says the user owns the rights to generations, except using them to train models. Terms also reference the Open RAIL-M license.
verdict: For 2D devs who need pixel-art sprites, rotations and animations; outputs are usable commercially on every plan, but its terms bar training other models on them.
bestFor: Pixel-art characters, rotations, animations and tilesets
freeTier: Free trial tier, no credit card

mcp.note: Remote MCP server for coding assistants (bearer token)

name: Retro Diffusion
summary: Pixel-art-specific image models for sprites, tiles, tilesets and animations, plus low-poly 3D model generation with export for Godot, Unity and Unreal. Also sells an Aseprite extension.
pricing: Pay per generation from a prepaid balance: images from $0.03 (RD Fast), $0.06, $0.18 (RD Pro); animations from $0.07 per clip. New accounts get a free starting balance.
license: Official FAQ: "Everything you generate is yours, for personal and commercial projects alike."
verdict: For pixel-art devs who want pay-per-image pricing with no subscription; the site says all output is yours for commercial use.
bestFor: Pay-per-image pixel-art sprites and tiles
freeTier: Free starting balance for new accounts

name: Scenario
summary: Production-focused generative platform for game art: train custom style models on your own assets, generate images, textures, 3D meshes, video and audio. API-first with Unity/Unreal integration.
pricing: Free tier with 50 daily credits. Starter $15/month, Pro $45/month, Max $75/month (monthly billing; annual saves 33%). Enterprise custom.
license: All paid plans include a full commercial license; free plan outputs are for personal and evaluation use only (per pricing FAQ).
verdict: For studios that want custom style models trained on their own art; commercial use needs a paid plan (free output is personal/evaluation only).
bestFor: Studios training custom style models on their own art

mcp.note: Hosted MCP server (OAuth or API key)

name: Leonardo.Ai
summary: General image and video generation platform with trainable custom models; usable for concept art, item icons and texture ideas.
pricing: Free: 150 fast tokens/day (public creations). Essential $12/month, Premium $30/month, Ultimate $60/month (ex. tax). Team and API plans available.
license: Paid subscribers retain full ownership and IP rights. Free tier: Leonardo holds rights to the images but grants you a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence for commercial use; free creations are public.
verdict: For general concept art and icon ideas; free-tier output can be used commercially but is public and Leonardo holds rights to it, while paid plans give you ownership.
bestFor: General concept art and icon ideas

api.note: API plans are separate from web subscriptions

mcp.note: Hosted MCP server (needs API plan and key)

name: Layer
summary: Generative content platform aimed at game studios: style-trained models, concept art, marketing creatives and asset variations with team workflows.
pricing: Start for free. Subscriptions begin at $10/month for 300 Creative Units, increasing by $60 per 1,000 CUs; $0 per seat.
license: Pricing page lists "Commercial license for all users". Free-tier scope: unverified.
verdict: For studios that want style-trained generation with no per-seat fees; the pricing page lists a commercial licence for all users.
bestFor: Style-consistent game art and marketing creatives

name: Ludo.ai
summary: Game ideation and asset tool: concept generation, sprites and sprite sheets, textures, plus a Unity editor plugin and API.
pricing: Free plan (sprite sheets watermarked). Indie $15/month ($180/year), Pro $35/month ($420/year), Studio $300/month ($3,600/year); credit packs from $15.
license: FAQ: the person who initiates a generation is recognized as the full owner of that content and can export and use it as they see fit.
verdict: For Unity devs who want ideation and 2D assets in one place; its FAQ says you own what you generate, but free-plan sprite sheets are watermarked.
bestFor: Game ideation plus 2D sprites in one tool

api.note: REST API on Pro or Studio plans

mcp.note: Remote MCP server on Pro or Studio plans

name: Meshy
summary: Text-to-3D and image-to-3D model generation with AI texturing; paid plans add animation with 600+ motions. DCC bridge listed for Roblox, Blender, Godot, Unity and Unreal.
pricing: Free: 100 monthly credits. Pro $20/month (1,000 credits). Higher tiers listed at $40 and $70 (Studio, team) per month; Enterprise custom.
license: Paid plans: you own the assets you create. Free plan: assets licensed to you under CC BY 4.0 (commercial use with attribution to Meshy).
verdict: For quick text- or image-to-3D props with Godot/Unity/Unreal bridges; free output is CC BY 4.0, so you must credit Meshy unless you pay.
bestFor: Quick text- or image-to-3D props with texturing and rigging
exportFormats: GLB, FBX, OBJ, USDZ, BLEND, STL, 3MF (API target formats)

name: Tripo AI
summary: Text/image/multi-view to 3D model generation with retopology, segmentation and up to 4K/8K texture generation. DCC bridge lists Blender, Unity, Unreal, Godot and others.
pricing: Free: 200 monthly credits. Pro $20/month billed annually ($240/yr). Max $90/month billed annually. Team $55/seat/month billed annually.
license: Pricing page: Free plan = "Public Models · Non-Commercial Use"; Pro, Max and Team = "Private Models · Commercial Use".
verdict: For 3D models with retopology and engine bridges; the free plan is non-commercial, so shipping assets requires a paid plan.
bestFor: Text/image-to-3D with retopology on paid plans

name: Hyper3D Rodin
summary: Rodin generates 3D models from text or images, with options like high-poly quad meshes; the platform also lists HDRI and texture generators.
pricing: Free tier ($0; direct credits $1.5 each). Creator $30/month ($24/month yearly). Business $120/month ($96/month yearly). Enterprise custom.
license: Business plan lists "Commercial license included"; FAQ says paid plans include broader export and usage rights. Exact rights on Free and Creator: unverified.
verdict: For high-detail 3D generation; commercial rights on the Free and Creator tiers are unverified, so check its terms before you ship.
bestFor: High-detail 3D generation with quad-mesh options

name: Sloyd
summary: Template-based and AI 3D generator for game-ready props and objects, with browser editor and plugins for Unity, Unreal and Blender on paid plans.

license: Free plan: personal-use license. Plus and Pro include a commercial license (you own what you generate; Pro adds reselling).
verdict: For game-ready props from editable templates with Unity/Unreal plugins; the free plan is personal-use only.
bestFor: Template-based game-ready props

name: Cascadeur
summary: Physics-based keyframe animation software with AI-assisted autoposing, inbetweening and mocap cleanup; exports FBX, DAE, USD and glTF on paid plans.

name: DeepMotion Animate 3D
summary: Markerless AI motion capture: turns ordinary video into 3D character animation; sister product SayMotion does text-to-motion.
pricing: Freemium (free, no card). Starter $9, Innovator $17, Professional $39, Studio $83 per month, paid annually.
license: Freemium accounts are for personal, non-commercial use; a premium subscription plan is required for licensed (commercial) animation.
verdict: For turning reference video into 3D animation cheaply; the free Freemium tier is non-commercial only.
bestFor: Turning reference video into 3D animation

summary: AI motion capture from video plus text-to-motion clips, exported via Rokoko Studio as FBX/BVH for Unity, Unreal, Blender and other tools.
